title: The Late Songbook
premise: Silas Pemberton has built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days while keeping her own heart locked in the past tense, ever since her sister's death and a letter she never sent. When an estate sale turns up that letter—postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to the man she loved and abandoned—she must track him down before he learns the truth from anyone but her. Along the way she's pulled into the orbit of a ragtag wedding crew who become the family she never let herself have. In the end, Silas delivers the letter herself, forgives the person in the mirror, and chooses to stop merely surviving love and start living it.
about_author: Lior Yarrow spent a decade writing obituaries for a small coastal paper before turning to fiction, which explains a lifelong fascination with what people leave unsaid. She lives above a shuttered ballroom with two cats named after failed marriages.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: In Silas's POV, we open mid-wedding: flawless, joyless, and secretly hers to rescue when the florist quits at noon. That night, sorting a deceased client's estate, she finds her own unsent letter—returned, unopened, postmarked eleven years ago. The emotional beat is dread disguised as control; Silas realizes the past tense she lives in has just been revoked.

chapters.title: The Crew of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Still Silas's POV: she hires a misfit crew—a disgraced chef, a teenage runaway DJ, a widowed officiant—to cover her busiest season while she searches for Theo, the letter's addressee. Their chaotic warmth keeps cracking her armor. Rising tension builds as she discovers Theo never left town; he's been nearby all along, and someone on her crew knows him.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Knew
chapters.summary: Climax. Silas finally confronts Theo, who reveals he wrote back years ago—and his reply was intercepted by her late sister, who feared losing Silas to a life away from home. POV shifts briefly to Theo for the confrontation's turn. Betrayal, grief, and fury collide as Silas must decide whether her survival strategy was protection or self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Late Songbook
chapters.summary: Resolution, Silas's POV. At the season's final wedding—the runaway DJ's estranged mother remarrying—Silas hands over not the old letter but a new one, read aloud, forgiving herself first. Theo doesn't promise forever; he promises Tuesdays. The found family toasts her, and Silas, for once, stays for the last song.
